tex_content.label: W_3fordiff
tex_content.source:
\label{W_3fordiff}

Let $({\mathcal M},G)$ be as in Theorem~\ref{MAIN}, let ${\mathcal X}$ be a
path of components on $[t_0,t_1]$ with
$\pi_2({\mathcal X}(t_0))=0$, and let
$0\ne\xi\in\pi_3({\mathcal X}(t_0),*)$. Then
\[
\frac{dW_\xi}{dt}(t)\le-2\pi-\frac12R_{\min}(t)W_\xi(t)
\]
in the sense of forward difference quotients. The function is continuous at
nonsurgery times and satisfies
$W_\xi(t)\le\liminf_{t'\to t^-}W_\xi(t')$ at surgery times.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
  \uses{prop:eventual-trivial-pi2, prop:w3-forward-difference-quotient, MAIN, lem:forward-difference-quotient}
\sketch Continuity and surgery semicontinuity are
Claims~\ref{claim:w-xi-continuity-nonsurgery} and
\ref{claim:w-xi-surgery-semicontinuity}. On a surgery-free interval, choose a
family within $\varepsilon$ of $W_\xi(t_0)$ and apply
Proposition~\ref{prop:curve-deformation-existence}. If the comparison solution
is nonnegative, Corollary~\ref{cor:short-loop-bounds-small-disk} controls the
short-loop alternative and gives $W_\xi(t_1)\le w(t_1)+o(1)$. If it is
negative, all non-short alternatives would have negative area, so every loop
would be short, contradicting Lemma~\ref{lem:short-loops-trivial-pi3}. Letting
$t_1\downarrow t_0$ gives the quotient inequality.
\end{proof}

The function is continuous at nonsurgery times and satisfies $W_\xi (t)\le \liminf _{t'\to t^-}W_\xi (t')$ at surgery times.
Proof

↗ prop:eventual-trivial-pi2 ↗ prop:w3-forward-difference-quotient ↗ MAIN ↗ lem:forward-difference-quotient \sketch Continuity and surgery semicontinuity are Claims 3 and 3. On a surgery-free interval, choose a family within $\varepsilon $ of $W_\xi (t_0)$ and apply Proposition 10. If the comparison solution is nonnegative, Corollary 4 controls the short-loop alternative and gives $W_\xi (t_1)\le w(t_1)+o(1)$. If it is negative, all non-short alternatives would have negative area, so every loop would be short, contradicting Lemma 4. Letting $t_1\downarrow t_0$ gives the quotient inequality.

dependencies.title: MAIN
dependencies.description:
\label{MAIN}

There are parameter sequences
\[
  {\bf K}=\{\kappa_i\},\qquad
  \Delta=\{\delta_i\},\qquad
  {\bf r}=\{r_i\}
\]
such that, for the step function $r(t)=r_i$ on each prescribed interval, every
nonincreasing positive $\overline\delta(t)\leq\Delta$ has the following
property. Any Ricci flow with surgery on $[0,T)$ satisfying Assumptions
(1)--(7), positive pinching, the strong $(C,\epsilon)$-canonical-neighborhood
assumption with parameter ${\bf r}$, and ${\bf K}$-noncollapsing extends to a
flow on $[0,\infty)$ satisfying all the same conditions.
\end{theorem}
